batch_note: No letter or first-letter pattern predicts the key: keys are balanced (10/10/10/10), and each cohort's options share one initial-letter family (A c/b, B p/r, C d-g, D i-n, E s-w) that is identical for key and distractors. Two repeated TEMPLATES, neither predictive without the passage: (1) 'X calls the Y the Z's ___' figurative-noun items (A-02, A-03, A-08, B-05, B-06, B-07, C-03, C-04, D-02, D-04, E-01, E-04, E-07, E-08) and 'the agent had ___ the thing' verb items (the rest); (2) every distractor gets a planted surface lure plus one planted refuting detail (e.g. cafeteria/seed A-02, pageant/hats and roundup/ponies B-06, pharmacy/bottles and parlor/stove room B-07, tollbooth/buoys E-01, thermometer/frozen-and-hot decades E-04), often in a trailing sentence after the blank (C-01, C-05, C-08, D-01, D-02, D-05, D-06, D-08). A test-wise student could learn that the option a dangling post-blank sentence refutes is never the key, which narrows by one option in those eight items; worth a variety note for the next brief.
